燕京，菊儿胡同。周日，清晨的第一缕阳光落在屋脊的破瓦上，破瓦枯草之中，间杂着几株绿芽。伴随着第一道屋门被推开，大杂院鸡零狗碎的生活又开始了。
1979年的春天，跟往常相比，微不可查的改变也开始在大杂院里悄然发生。人们虽然嘴上在讨论着“改革”，讨论着从报纸看到的新讨论，以及可能出现的新政策，但心里又有一种不真实的感觉。
毕竟政策离自己太远，讨论得再热烈，也得回到鸡毛蒜皮的现实当中。
如果说新政策的讨论范围小且普通人难以捉摸的话，那么南疆发生的战事，哪怕是只读小学的学生、不认识字的老大爷，都能聊上一嘴。
因为刘济民，大杂院的居民早上醒来第一件事是跑胡同口的厕所；第二件事则是在厕所里看报纸。
有时候送报员来的晚，他们就在厕所里品昨天的报纸。
“老王，昨个儿歇好了没？”梁婶看到王爱梅后，立即快走几步到了王爱梅旁边。
王爱梅顶着黑眼圈，使劲扯着嘴角，露出一丝笑容道：“还行，睡得还行，你呢！”
“我也还行，上了年纪了，觉不多。”梁婶儿看了一眼王爱梅，脸上的笑容稍微收了收，“老王，你也别担心，济民这孩子吉人自有天相。不是宣布撤军了吗？估计这两天就有信儿了！”
王爱梅点头，笃定道：“我家老二肯定没事儿！”
“对，子弹都躲着济民走。放宽心，你跟你家那口子别太担心了！”梁婶儿道。
“行，我回了，得赶紧做饭了。”
“得嘞，我也得赶紧回了！”
王爱梅走回大杂院，跟周围的邻居点头示意。大家都知道刘济民上了前线，就连平时不对付的，也没人触王爱梅的霉头。
“王姨，我家炸油条，一会儿让您尝尝。”李春燕笑道。
王爱梅道：“行，我晚上蒸馒头，你给你奶奶拿两个，上了年纪，刚出锅的馒头吃着软乎。”
“好嘞！”李春燕笑着开始忙活了起来。
屋内，刘振国刚醒就打开收音机在听新闻。他尤其想听127师的消息，但是电台一般不会播得这么细致，除非是典型事件。

Yanjing, Juer Hutong. On Sunday, the first ray of sunshine in the early morning fell on the broken tiles on the roof. There were a few green shoots among the withered grass on the broken tiles. As the first door of the house was pushed open, the messy life in the courtyard began again.
In the spring of 1979, compared with usual times, subtle changes began to occur quietly in the courtyard. Although people are talking about "reform", the new discussions seen in newspapers, and possible new policies, there is a feeling of unreality in their hearts.
After all, the policy is too far away from us. No matter how passionate the discussion is, we have to return to the trivial reality.
If the discussion scope of the new policy is small and elusive to ordinary people, then the war in southern Xinjiang can be discussed by even elementary school students and illiterate old men.
Because of Liu Jimin, the first thing the residents of Dazayuan did when they woke up in the morning was to run to the toilet at the entrance of the alley; the second thing was to read newspapers in the toilet.
Sometimes the newspaper delivery boy came late, so they would read yesterday's newspaper in the toilet.
"Old Wang, have you rested yesterday?" After Aunt Liang saw Wang Aimei, she immediately walked a few steps to Wang Aimei's side.
Wang Aimei faced the dark circles under her eyes, pulled the corners of her mouth hard, showed a smile and said: "It's okay, I slept okay, how about you!"
"I'm okay. I'm getting old and I don't sleep much." Aunt Liang glanced at Wang Aimei and the smile on her face faded slightly. "Old Wang, don't worry. This kid Jimin has his own destiny. Didn't he announce the withdrawal? I guess there will be news in the next two days!"
Wang Aimei nodded and said firmly: "My second child must be fine!"
"Yes, the bullets are all avoiding Jimin. Relax, you and your family don't worry too much!" Aunt Liang said.
"Okay, I'm back, I have to cook quickly."
"Okay, I have to go back quickly!"
Wang Aimei walked back to the courtyard and nodded to the neighbors around her. Everyone knew that Liu Jimin was on the front line, and no one, even those he didn't usually deal with, had trouble with Wang Aimei.
"Aunt Wang, I'll let you try my fried dough sticks later." Li Chunyan said with a smile.
Wang Aimei said: "Okay, I'll steam the steamed buns tonight, and you can get two for your grandma. She's old, and the steamed buns just out of the oven will be soft to eat."
"Okay!" Li Chunyan smiled and started to work.
Inside the house, Liu Zhenguo turned on the radio and listened to the news as soon as he woke up. He especially wanted to hear news about the 127th Division, but the radio station usually wouldn't broadcast it in such detail unless it was a typical incident.
